title: I'd like to invite you
goal: Invite Sēf to dinner at your flat, and say yes warmly when he asks you a favour
tip: ḥabbēt is a polite 'I'd like to'. Put a bare present verb after it, as after abi: ḥabbēt aʿazmak 'I'd like to invite you', ḥabbēt aṭbakh 'I'd like to cook'. It sounds softer than abi, and a woman says it the same way.
dialogue: B
هلا سيف! حبيت أعزمك على العشا يوم الخميس
hala Sēf! ḥabbēt aʿazmak ʿala l-ʿasha yōm il-khamīs
Hi Sēf! I'd like to invite you to dinner on Thursday.
A
هلا فيك! على هالخشم. وين العزيمة؟
hala fīk! ʿala hal-khashm. wēn il-ʿazīma?
Hi! With pleasure. Where's the dinner?
B
في شقتي. تقدر تقول لفهد بعد؟
fi shiggti. tigdar tgūl l-Fahad baʿad?
At my flat. Can you tell Fahad too?
A
أبشر! بس سوي لنا كرك بعد العشا
abshir! bas sawwī-lna karak baʿd il-ʿasha
You got it! But make us karak after dinner.
B
على راسي! وحبيت أطبخ لكم أكل بريطاني
ʿala rāsi! w ḥabbēt aṭbakh-lkum akil brīṭāni
Gladly! And I'd like to cook you (all) some British food.
A
أكل بريطاني؟ إن شاء الله زين!
akil brīṭāni? in shāʼ allāh zēn!
British food? Let's hope it's good!
items: I'd like to (+ verb), I wanted to (polite)
a woman says the same; ḥabbēt agūl-lak = I wanted to tell you; on its own it also means 'I liked, I loved'
I'd like to invite you (to a man)
to a woman: ḥabbēt aʿazmich (حبيت أعزمج)
the invitation; the dinner or lunch you're invited to
with pleasure, gladly (lit. on this nose)
a warm yes to an invitation or a favour
you got it, consider it done (to a man)
to a woman: abshiri (أبشري); the answer to a request, to friends and elders alike
to a woman the same: sawwī-lna
gladly, at your service (lit. on my head)
the answer to a favour someone asks of you
culture: Gulf hosts insist, often with wallāh. To turn something down politely, say mashkūr, allāh ykhallīk, or il-marra l-yāya 'next time'. To say yes to an invitation or a favour, ʿala hal-khashm and ʿala rāsi are warm, very Gulf answers.

title: I'd love to, but…
goal: Maryam invites you to lunch with the team: say you'd love to, explain why you may be late, and ask for the address
tip: widdi + a bare verb is 'I'd love to': widdi ashūf il-jamāʿa 'I'd love to see everyone'. It's softer than abi, so it's good for a kind no: widdi wallāh, bas… 'I'd really love to, but…'. To ask: widdak? to a man, widdich? to a woman.
grammar: widdi + verb 'I'd love to'; widdak? 'would you like to?'
dialogue: A
باكر بنتغدى كلنا سوا. ودك تيي؟
bāchir binitghadda killna sawa. widdak tiyi?
Tomorrow we're all having lunch together. Would you like to come?
B
ودي والله، بس عندي امتحان الساعة ثنتين
widdi wallāh, bas ʿindi imtiḥān is-sāʿa thintēn
I'd really love to, but I've got an exam at two.
A
خسارة! وبعد الامتحان؟ نحن في المطعم اللي صوب المكتب
khasāra! w baʿd il-imtiḥān? niḥin fi l-maṭʿam illi ṣōb il-maktab
Shame! What about after the exam? We'll be at the restaurant near the office.
B
إن شاء الله. ودي أشوف الجماعة كلهم
in shāʼ allāh. widdi ashūf il-jamāʿa killhum
God willing. I'd love to see everyone.
A
إن شاء الله يعني هيه، ولّا يعني لا؟
in shāʼ allāh yaʿni hē, walla yaʿni la?
Does 'in shāʼ allāh' mean yes, or does it mean no?
B
يعني هيه! بس يمكن أتأخر. تطرشين لي العنوان؟
yaʿni hē! bas yimkin atʼakhkhar. tṭarrishīn-li l-ʿinwān?
It means yes! But I might be late. Will you send me the address?
A
أكيد. ونترياك!
akīd. w nitrayyāk!
Of course. And we'll wait for you!
items: a kind way to say no
would you like to come? (to a man)
to a woman: widdich tiyīn? (ودج تيين؟)
widdi ashūfak = I'd love to see you
it means yes, I mean yes
will you send me (to a woman)
we'll wait for you (to a man)
culture: in shāʼ allāh 'God willing' goes with every plan, and people mean it. It can also be a polite, non-committal 'maybe'. So if you really mean yes, add something firm: in shāʼ allāh, akīd 'definitely', or name a time.

title: Let's go to the desert
goal: Suggest a desert trip to Sēf, ask if you can bring a friend, and ask to come back early
tip: khal + a we-verb is a quick 'let's': khal nrūḥ 'let's go', khal nshūf 'let's see'. It means the same as khallna nrūḥ. yṣīr? asks 'is it OK?': yṣīr ayīb rbīʿi? 'can I bring my friend?'. The answer is yṣīr 'it's fine' or ma yṣīr 'no way'.
dialogue: A
يوم السبت شو نسوي؟
yōm is-sabt shu nsawwi?
What shall we do on Saturday?
B
خل نروح البر! الجو حلو هالأيام
khal nrūḥ il-barr! il-jaww ḥilu hal-ayyām
Let's go to the desert! The weather's nice these days.
A
والله فكرة! خل نقول لفهد بعد
wallāh fikra! khal ngūl l-Fahad baʿad
Good idea! Let's tell Fahad too.
B
زين. ويصير أييب ربيعي مارك؟
zēn. w yṣīr ayīb rbīʿi Mārk?
Great. And is it OK if I bring my friend Mark?
A
أكيد يصير! في مكان في السيارة
akīd yṣīr! fī makān fi s-sayyāra
Of course! There's room in the car.
B
بس يصير نرجع بدري؟ لازم أذاكر
bas yṣīr nirjaʿ badri? lāzim adhākir
But can we come back early? I have to revise.
A
ما يصير! خل نشوف، يمكن نرجع الساعة عشر
ma yṣīr! khal nshūf, yimkin nirjaʿ is-sāʿa ʿashr
No way! Let's see, maybe we'll be back at ten.
items: khal ngūl l-Fahad = let's tell Fahad
is it OK? can I? can we?
yṣīr ayīb…? = can I bring…?; answer: yṣīr, or ma yṣīr
no way, that won't do; it's not right
ma fī makān = there's no room
I have to revise, I have to study

title: Let's finish it first
goal: Plan the afternoon with Maryam at the office, then suggest karak to the whole team
tip: khallna 'let's' changes with who you talk to: khallīna to a woman, khallūna to a group. The next verb takes n- for 'we': khallūna niṭlaʿ 'let's head out' (to a group). You'll also hear khallīna said to men.
grammar: khallīna (to a woman), khallūna (to a group) + verb
dialogue: A
سالم، المدير يبي الملف اليوم!
Sālim, il-mudīr yabi l-malaff il-yōm!
Sālim, the manager wants the file today!
B
زين، خلينا نخلص قبل الغدا
zēn, khallīna nkhalliṣ gabil il-ghada
OK, let's finish before lunch.
A
خلنا نبدا الحين. أنا أكتب وانت تطالع
khallna nibda l-ḥīn. ana aktib w inta tṭāliʿ
Let's start now. I'll write and you check it.
B
أوكي. والشباب دوم يشربون كرك بعد الشغل
ōkē. w ish-shabāb dōm yishrabūn karak baʿd ish-shughul
OK. And the guys always have karak after work.
A
فكرة حلوة! خل نقول للجماعة كلهم
fikra ḥilwa! khal ngūl lil-jamāʿa killhum
Nice idea! Let's tell the whole team.
B
يا جماعة! خلونا نطلع الساعة خمس
yā jamāʿa! khallūna niṭlaʿ is-sāʿa khams
Everyone! Let's head out at five.
A
بس أول خلنا نخلص الملف!
bas awwal khallna nkhalliṣ il-malaff!
But first let's finish the file!
items: to a man: khallna (خلنا); to a group: khallūna (خلونا); you'll also hear khallīna said to men
to one man: khallna; to one woman: khallīna
to a man: khallna nkhalliṣ; nkhallṣah = we finish it
let's head out, let's go out (to a group)
you look at, you check (to a man)

title: Checkpoint 2.4: lunch at Bū Rāshid's
goal: Bū Rāshid phones to invite you to Friday lunch: answer respectfully, ask to bring Fahad, and promise not to be late
tip: With an elder, stay respectful: yā ʿammi, ṭāl ʿumrak, and abshir for 'consider it done'. For a group, -kum and -ūn come back: killkum 'all of you', la titʼakhkharūn 'don't be late', nshūfkum 'we'll see you all'. widdna is 'we'd love to'.
grammar: checkpoint 2.4: recycle s2u055–s2u071 (elders, invitations, ḥabbēt, widdi, yṣīr)
dialogue: A
السلام عليكم يا سالم. شحالك؟
as-salāmu ʿalaykum yā Sālim. shḥālak?
Peace be upon you, Sālim. How are you?
B
وعليكم السلام! بخير الله يسلمك. شحالك يا عمي؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām! b-khēr allāh ysallmak. shḥālak yā ʿammi?
And upon you! Fine, thank you. How are you, sir?
A
الحمد لله. حبيت أعزمك على الغدا يوم الجمعة
il-ḥamdu lillāh. ḥabbēt aʿazmak ʿala l-ghada yōm il-jumʿa
Thank God. I'd like to invite you to lunch on Friday.
B
على هالخشم! يصير أييب فهد ويانا؟
ʿala hal-khashm! yṣīr ayīb Fahad wiyyāna?
With pleasure! May I bring Fahad with us?
A
أكيد! تعالوا كلكم، بس لا تتأخرون
akīd! taʿālu killkum, bas la titʼakhkharūn
Of course! Come, all of you, just don't be late.
B
أبشر طال عمرك! ودنا نشوفك
abshir ṭāl ʿumrak! widdna nshūfak
Of course, sir! We'd love to see you.
A
الله يحفظكم. نشوفكم يوم الجمعة إن شاء الله
allāh yiḥfaẓkum. nshūfkum yōm il-jumʿa in shāʼ allāh
God keep you all. See you all on Friday, God willing.
items: to one man: la titʼakhkhar; to one woman: la titʼakhkharīn
to an elder or someone senior
widdna nshūfak = we'd love to see you
God keep you all (warm thanks or goodbye)
we'll see you all, see you (to a group)
to one man: nshūfak; to one woman: nshūfich

title: Are you upset?
goal: Maryam looks upset at work: ask what's wrong and cheer her up
tip: Feeling words agree with the person: zaʿlān (a man), zaʿlāna (a woman). With kān they go into the past: kint zaʿlāna 'I was upset' (a woman). illi links a verb to a noun: il-ʿarẓ illi sawwētah 'the presentation I did'. ṣij? is 'really?'.
grammar: recycle: kān + feeling word; illi + verb
dialogue: A
صباح الخير
ṣabāḥ il-khēr
Good morning.
B
صباح النور! خير؟ انتي زعلانة؟
ṣabāḥ in-nūr! khēr? inti zaʿlāna?
Good morning! Everything OK? Are you upset?
A
هيه شوي. المدير ما حب العرض اللي سويته
hē shwayy. il-mudīr ma ḥabb il-ʿarẓ illi sawwētah
A bit, yes. The manager didn't like the presentation I did.
B
صج؟ بس العرض كان وايد زين!
ṣij? bas il-ʿarẓ kān wāyid zēn!
Really? But the presentation was really good!
A
والله؟ أنا كنت زعلانة من الصبح
wallāh? ana kint zaʿlāna min iṣ-ṣubḥ
Really? I've been upset since this morning.
B
لا تزعلين. يمكن المدير كان تعبان اليوم
la tizʿalīn. yimkin il-mudīr kān taʿbān il-yōm
Don't be upset. Maybe the manager was just tired today.
A
يمكن. الحين أحسن، الحمد لله
yimkin. il-ḥīn aḥsan, il-ḥamdu lillāh
Maybe. I feel better now, thank God.
items: a woman: zaʿlāna (زعلانة); zaʿlān min = upset with
to a man: la tizʿal (لا تزعل)
she didn't like: ma ḥabbat (ما حبت)

title: Calm down!
goal: Sēf is angry in the car park: calm him down and find out what's really wrong
tip: Use kān and illi to say what's behind a feeling: il-imtiḥān illi kān ams 'the exam (that was) yesterday'. mʿaṣṣib is 'angry' (a woman: mʿaṣṣba). allāh yihdāk 'God guide you' is a gentle 'come on now' to a friend who's overdoing it.
dialogue: A
شوف هذا! أخذ مكاني! ما صارت!
shūf hādha! khadh makāni! ma ṣārat!
Look at him! He took my spot! This is too much!
B
لا تعصب يا ريّال. في مكان ثاني هناك
la tʿaṣṣib yā rayyāl. fī makān thāni hnāk
Calm down, mate. There's another spot over there.
A
كل يوم جي! أنا معصب من الصبح
kill yōm chī! ana mʿaṣṣib min iṣ-ṣubḥ
It's like this every day! I've been angry since this morning.
B
ليش معصب؟ شو اللي صار؟
lēsh mʿaṣṣib? shu illi ṣār?
Why are you angry? What happened?
A
الامتحان اللي كان أمس، ما نجحت فيه
il-imtiḥān illi kān ams, ma nijaḥt fīh
The exam yesterday: I didn't pass it.
B
الله يهداك! امتحان واحد بس. المرة الياية إن شاء الله
allāh yihdāk! imtiḥān wāḥid bas. il-marra l-yāya in shāʼ allāh
Come on now! It's just one exam. Next time, God willing.
A
صح كلامك. خلاص، ما بعصب
ṣaḥḥ kalāmak. khalāṣ, ma baʿaṣṣib
You're right. OK, I won't get angry.
items: calm down, don't get angry (to a man)
to a woman: la tʿaṣṣbīn (لا تعصبين)
why are you angry? (to a man)
this is too much! this has gone too far!
said when something keeps happening or someone overdoes it
come on now (gentle telling-off, lit. God guide you) (to a man)
to a woman: allāh yihdāch (الله يهداج); to friends, not to elders
I didn't pass; you didn't pass (to a man)
to a woman: ma nijaḥti (ما نجحتي)
to a woman: ṣaḥḥ kalāmich (صح كلامج)

title: I was scared, now I'm happy
goal: Tell Sēf how your presentation went: how nervous you were and how happy you are now
tip: kint + a feeling word is 'I was …': kint khāyif 'I was scared'. The word agrees with the person: khāyif / khāyfa, mistānis / mistānsa. khāyif min is 'scared of'; khāyif ʿala is 'worried about (someone)'.
dialogue: A
شو صار في العرض اليوم؟
shu ṣār fi l-ʿarẓ il-yōm?
What happened with the presentation today?
B
كنت خايف من المدير، بس العرض كان زين!
kint khāyif min il-mudīr, bas il-ʿarẓ kān zēn!
I was scared of the manager, but the presentation went well!
A
قلت لك: لا تخاف! وشو قال المدير؟
gilt-lak: la tkhāf! w shu gāl il-mudīr?
I told you: don't worry! And what did the manager say?
B
قال: حلو وايد! والله وايد مستانس
gāl: ḥilu wāyid! wallāh wāyid mistānis
He said: really nice! I'm so happy.
A
مبروك! الليلة العشا على حسابي
mabrūk! il-lēla l-ʿasha ʿala ḥsābi
Congratulations! Tonight dinner's on me.
B
الله يبارك فيك! وانت بعد كنت خايف علي؟
allāh ybārik fīk! w inta baʿad kint khāyif ʿalay?
Thanks! And were you worried about me too?
A
شوي! بس الحين أنا بعد مستانس
shwayy! bas il-ḥīn ana baʿad mistānis
A bit! But now I'm happy too.
items: I was scared; you were scared (to a man)
a woman says: kint khāyfa; to a woman: kinti khāyfa
don't worry, don't be scared (to a man)
to a woman: la tkhāfīn (لا تخافين)
happy, pleased, having a good time (a man)
what did she say?: shu gālat?

title: Khēba!
goal: Sēf teases you about your big meal: tease him back the way friends do
tip: Friends tease, and the replies are short: khēba! 'seriously?!' to poke fun, ḥarām ʿalēk! 'that's not fair!' to protest, amzaḥ wiyyāk 'I'm joking'. kān still helps: hādhāk kān ghada 'that was lunch'.
dialogue: A
خيبة! بتاكل كل هذا؟
khēba! bitākil kill hādha?
Seriously?! You're going to eat all that?
B
حرام عليك! ما كلت شي من الصبح
ḥarām ʿalēk! ma kalt shay min iṣ-ṣubḥ
That's not fair! I haven't eaten anything since this morning.
A
أمزح وياك! بالعافية
amzaḥ wiyyāk! bil-ʿāfya
I'm joking! Enjoy your food.
B
الله يعافيك. وانت أمس كلت صحنين!
allāh yʿāfīk. w inta ams kalt ṣaḥnēn!
Thanks. And you ate two plates yesterday!
A
تمزح؟ هذاك كان غدا وعشا!
timzaḥ? hādhāk kān ghada w ʿasha!
Are you kidding? That was lunch and dinner!
B
خيبة! يلا، خلنا ناكل قبل لا يبرد
khēba! yalla, khallna nākil gabil la yibrad
Seriously?! Come on, let's eat before it gets cold.
items: pokes fun at someone overdoing it, or sounds unimpressed; never with strangers or elders
that's not fair! come on! (to a man)
to a woman: ḥarām ʿalēch (حرام عليج)
to a woman: amzaḥ wiyyāch (أمزح وياج)
culture: Friends in the Gulf tease each other a lot, and khēba 'seriously?!' is part of it: it pokes fun at someone overdoing it (khēba, you'll eat all that?) or says you're not impressed. Keep it for friends your own age. With strangers, elders or at work it sounds rude.
